transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

What finally scared me into making this appointment is that I’ve been having thoughts like… if I didn’t wake up tomorrow, maybe that would be easier. I don’t want to hurt myself, but those thoughts have been bothering me.
How long have you been feeling this way—having these low moods and thoughts about not wanting to wake up?
About six months, I think. It’s been this low, flat feeling for that long—my art classes and morning walks don’t feel restorative anymore.
Have you ever had a period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, quite different from your normal self?

Yes—there was a stretch where I had a lot more energy after work. I couldn’t really sit still. I kept sketching ideas for the store, reorganizing shelves at home, and signing up for extra training I didn’t actually need.
How many days in a row did that period of increased energy and reduced need for rest last?
It’s been about two months now, since the trouble with the new district manager really started. The mood and energy have been going up and down through that whole time.

During that two-month stretch of high energy, did you also notice sad or hopeless feelings happening at the very same time as the extra energy and racing thoughts, or did the low mood and the high-energy periods occur at completely separate times?
I’m not sure I can separate it that neatly. It’s felt like things have been up and down over those two months, but I don’t know whether they were happening at exactly the same time.

Thinking about a specific low, hopeless day in the past two months—on that same day, were you also experiencing racing thoughts or bursts of extra energy, or did the low mood happen on days when you felt calm and low-energy overall?
Most mornings lately I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling—like the color has drained out of everything before I even get dressed for the store.
Right now, during these heavy, low-energy mornings, are you also noticing things like racing thoughts, needing less sleep than usual, or bursts of restless energy at the same time?
I’m not really sure. In the mornings I mostly just notice that heavy feeling. I haven’t paid close attention to whether those other things are happening at the same time.
Are you still experiencing any of that increased energy, reduced need for sleep, or restlessness right now, or did those feelings stop before this current heavy, low mood started?
For a while, yes, I had this burst of energy after work. I couldn’t sit still—I’d sketch out ideas for the store, reorganize shelves at home, and sign up for extra training I didn’t really need.
Is that burst of extra energy and reduced need for sleep still happening right now, alongside your current low, heavy mood, or did it stop before this heavy feeling began?
For a while I did have that extra energy after work—I just couldn’t sit still. I was constantly making plans for the store, rearranging things at home, signing up for trainings I didn’t really need.
Thinking back, did that burst of extra energy and reduced need for sleep completely stop before this current heavy, low mood started, or is it still happening right alongside the low mood today?
It was going on for a while after work. I just couldn’t sit still—I kept coming up with store ideas, reorganizing things at home, and signing up for trainings I didn’t really need.
Right now, this week, are you still noticing that restless energy or trouble sitting still, or has that completely gone away while the low, heavy mood has been present?

It hasn’t completely gone away. Some days I find myself pacing around the living room and picking at my cuticles. Other days, though, even walking from the break room to the sales floor feels strangely slow.

On the days when you notice yourself pacing or feeling restless, are you also feeling that heavy, hopeless low mood at the very same time, or do the restless days and the heavy, low days tend to be different days?

It seems to vary. Some days I’m pacing around the living room and picking at my cuticles, and other days I feel so slowed down that even walking from the break room to the sales floor feels strangely slow.
